From 889b0e2721e793eb46cf7d17b965aa3252af3ec8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alper Ak <alperyasinak1@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 13:30:42 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] crypto: ccp - Fix use-after-free on error path

In the error path of sev_tsm_init_locked(), the code dereferences 't'
after it has been freed with kfree(). The pr_err() statement attempts
to access t->tio_en and t->tio_init_done after the memory has been
released.

Move the pr_err() call before kfree(t) to access the fields while the
memory is still valid.

This issue reported by Smatch static analyser

Fixes:4be423572da1 ("crypto/ccp: Implement SEV-TIO PCIe IDE (phase1)")
Signed-off-by: Alper Ak <alperyasinak1@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Tom Lendacky <thomas.lendacky@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>

diff --git a/drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev-tsm.c b/drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev-tsm.c
index adc9542ae806..b07ae529b591 100644
--- a/drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev-tsm.c
+++ b/drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev-tsm.c
@@ -378,9 +378,9 @@ void sev_tsm_init_locked(struct sev_device *sev, void *tio_status_page)
 	return;
 
 error_exit:
-	kfree(t);
 	pr_err("Failed to enable SEV-TIO: ret=%d en=%d initdone=%d SEV=%d\n",
 	       ret, t->tio_en, t->tio_init_done, boot_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_SEV));
+	kfree(t);
 }
 
 void sev_tsm_uninit(struct sev_device *sev)
-- 
2.34.1

This patch fixes a use-after-free bug in the error path of `sev_tsm_init_locked()` in `drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev-tsm.c`.

**Modification in the file:**
- In the `error_exit` label, the order of two statements is swapped: `pr_err()` (which accesses `t->tio_en` and `t->tio_init_done`) now executes **before** `kfree(t)`, instead of after.

**Relationship between modifications:**
- The original code called `kfree(t)` first, freeing the memory pointed to by `t`, and then attempted to print fields of the already-freed structure via `pr_err()`. This caused a use-after-free vulnerability. The fix ensures that the error message reads the structure fields while the memory is still valid, eliminating the bug.

In the error path of sev_tsm_init_locked(), the code called kfree(t) before using t->tio_en and t->tio_init_done in the pr_err() statement, leading to a use-after-free access to freed memory.

       ret, t->tio_en, t->tio_init_done, boot_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_SEV));

Reason:
The function kfree(t) releases the memory pointed to by t. Immediately after, pr_err() attempts to read t->tio_en and t->tio_init_done from the freed memory, causing a use-after-free access.

       ret, t->tio_en, t->tio_init_done, boot_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_SEV));
kfree(t);

Reason:
By moving pr_err() before kfree(t), the fields t->tio_en and t->tio_init_done are accessed while the memory is still valid, eliminating the use-after-free error.
